What gets me so much here is how many people could have stopped this before it got to this point, whether social services, doctors, etc... The US truly is run like a bunch of little city states in Rome, each doing their own thing. There were red flags all over, but they probably looked like far less and more innocuous because each state only looks at their own. This woman should have had someone stepping in before this got this bad. I understand that sometimes folks do commit petty crimes to get a place to sleep for the night, it's heartbreaking. Again, richest country in the world, but every city has a huge problem w homelessness, mental health and addiction. Frustrating to see how not only Margot and Julian but Bionca were failed by the system. She should have been in a care facility it's quite clear. 
My Uncle suffered schizophrenia, and lived at a mental health facility for many years. In fact, he did well there and improved. Then the place was shut down and the patients were literally abandoned for the most part. Those who had family to step in were lucky. My uncle didn't at the time, or at least he was lead to believe he didn't, and ended up homeless for many years. 
Most people with schizophrenia are more likely a danger to themselves than others. Bionca is a fringe case, and as is clear while her reasoning was clearly impaired, it wasn't 'because of the disease', in that she was not prompted to kill by voices or hallucinations. This was someone with severely impaired thinking acting in a way that she thought in that state, would get her 'cared for' and she didn't care who she hurt. I doubt she was able to recognize that others COULD hurt.

This case is heartbreaking beyond words. My thoughts are first and foremost with the mother, father, and their family and friends. The loss of their beautiful little boy is pain that never heals. I know in my heart if something happened to my daughter I would most likely die. She 26 now but still my everything. 

I want to be very clear: nothing about mental illness justifies what happened, and I don’t have sympathy for her actions. But it’s also impossible to ignore that she was clearly not mentally well for most of her adult life. The record shows years of red flags, repeated encounters with police, doctors, hospitals, shelters, where she was actively asking for help and even trying to get arrested just to have somewhere safe to be.

That doesn’t excuse the crime. It does, however, expose how deeply broken our mental health system is in the United States. There were so many opportunities for intervention, treatment, or long-term care that never materialized. This tragedy wasn’t just the result of one person’s actions, it was the result of systemic failure, playing out over years, until the worst possible outcome occurred.

This is absolutely heartbreaking all the way around.

We can mourn the victims and acknowledge that this should never have been allowed to reach this point.

From an outsider perspective it’s very clear she was mentally ill. I have worked with people who are schizophrenic and yes, their mood swings can be very quick and their actions although seemingly organized still have aspects that show their plans aren’t thought out as a sane person would. She stole a knife and no one stopped her or noticed. She walked around with a large butcher knife in a busy shopping complex on a sunny afternoon and again , no one noticed. She made no attempt at any point to conceal her knife. No of her behaviors seem like normal decisions. Her choice of victim however is odd. There was an elderly man walking right near the woman and her son. I would argue he would have been vulnerable as well. I don’t think we can ever make sense of that choice because we don’t know why. Clearly she wanted help and sought it out as much as she had the resources for.

With all that being said, had she attacked my child and myself , I would not care about any of that. Throw her away for life. I don’t care how tough life was for her. I don’t care what she went through. I don’t have sympathy for her. I’m glad the mother got to face her and say I hate you. She should hate her. She is what we call evil. Poor baby boy. I can’t imagine the horrors his family goes through every single day and will forever because of her actions. 

I don’t blame the family for hating her. I do blame her for hurting such a small, precious baby. I do blame the mental health system in America for failing everyone in this case. It’s an absolute mess. 
I teach my daughter that when you are walking through a parking lot, head on a swivel. Who is next to you, who is behind you and who is in front of you. Is anyone around you acting strange. Look at people. If you see something odd, tell someone. Don’t expect other to notice because the clearly don’t.  Maybe it’s nothing, but better safe than sorry. We shouldn’t constantly have to feel this way but unfortunately it’s the world we live in.
